tagline: A big spring and a very short river on the Missouri.
intro: Giant Springs Road leaves River Drive at the edge of Great Falls and runs a little over two miles down the Missouri to the railroad tracks, with the River's Edge Trail alongside. Along the way are Giant Springs State Park and the Lewis and Clark Interpretive Center, and the road was moved slightly when the center was built. Across the water is Black Eagle, where the first dam on the Missouri went in in 1890.

This is the stretch where Lewis and Clark spent a month hauling their boats around the five Great Falls. On June 18, 1805, scouting the south bank, William Clark came on a spring he judged to be the largest in the world.

moments.title: Giant Springs
moments.text: More than 150 million gallons a day come up at a steady 54 degrees, snowmelt from the Little Belt Mountains that has spent some 3,000 years underground.

moments.title: Roe River
moments.text: The spring runs about 200 feet to the Missouri. A Great Falls fifth-grade class named it in a campaign begun in 1987 and got Guinness to list it as the world's shortest river.
